chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Thawir ibn Abi Fakhtah, from Abu Jamilyah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them) who said:

There are three ranks, three expiations, three destroyers, and three saviors. As for the ranks: spreading peace (greeting), feeding food, and praying at night while people are asleep. As for the expiations: perfecting ablution in the cold, walking by night and day to the prayers, and maintaining attendance at congregational prayers. As for the three destroyers: stinginess that is obeyed, desires that are followed, and a person's self-admiration. As for the saviors: fearing God in private and in public, moderation in wealth and poverty, and saying the word of justice when pleased and when angry.

key_terms.شُحٌّ مَطَاعٌ: Stinginess that is obeyed (acting on it)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that raise spiritual ranks and the three things that destroy faith according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) categorizes spiritual life into four triads, linking social etiquette with inner purification. The 'destroyers' (mubiqat) highlight how internal vices like self-admiration lead to ruin, while the 'saviors' (munjiyat) emphasize consistency in God-consciousness across all states of being. This structure reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing outward ritual observance with inward ethical integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-10 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Harun ibn al-Jahm, on the authority of Savir ibn AbiFakhteh, on the authority of Abi Jamileh al-Mufaz’zal ibn Salih, on the authority of Sa’ed ibn Tarif, on the authority of Abi Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), “

There are three ranks, three expiations, three things which destroy and three things which save. As for the three things which raise the ranks they are greeting aloud, feeding the needy, and praying in the night when the people are asleep. As for the three expiations, they are making ablutions with cold water, going on foot in the day and at night to the prayers, and attending congregational prayers. As for the three things which destroy, they are being really stingy, following selfish desires, and being haughty and selfish. As for the three things which save us, they are fearing God in private and in public; moderation in times of prosperity and poverty; and saying what is fair whether we are pleased or angry.”
